title: Establishing a nursery
competency: Select a suitable nursery site and describe how fruit seedlings are raised and managed.

keywords.def: A managed site where plants are cared for during their early growth stages.
The main root that grows straight down from the seed.

en.text: A nursery is a managed site where young plants get suitable conditions for germination and early growth until they are strong enough for the main field; young tropical seedlings need protection from strong sun, heavy rain, drought, pests and diseases. A good nursery site is gently sloping, has a continuous water supply, is protected from strong wind, is well drained and fertile, is separate from but near the main field, has dependable labour, is free from flooding and is not shaded by trees or buildings.

am.text: የችግኝ ጣቢያ ቦታ፡ ትንሽ ተዳፋት፣ ቋሚ ውሃ፣ ከንፋስ የተጠበቀ፣ ውሃ የማያቁር ለም አፈር፣ ከጎርፍና ከጥላ የራቀ መሆን አለበት።

screens.title: Pick a plot
screens.ask: Which plot would you choose for a fruit nursery?
opts: A gentle slope near a stream, behind a windbreak
A flat valley floor that floods each rainy season
A steep, windy hilltop far from water
Under big shade trees behind the school
screens.after: The gentle slope drains well, has water close by and is sheltered from wind.

screens.title: What a nursery is
paras: A nursery is a managed site for young plants.
It gives suitable conditions for germination and early growth.
Plants stay until they are strong enough for the main field.
Young tropical seedlings need shade from severe sun.
Heavy rain, drought, pests and diseases damage seedlings.

screens.title: Eight criteria for a nursery site
paras: 1. Gently sloping topography.
2. Continuous and sufficient water.
3. Protected from strong wind (or a good windbreak).
4. Well drained, fertile soil.
5. Separate from, but near, the main field.
6. Adequate, dependable labour.
7. Free from flooding.
8. Not shaded by trees or buildings.

screens.title: Key word
defs: A managed site where plants are cared for during their early growth stages.

screens.text: The purpose of a nursery is to
opts: give young plants suitable conditions for germination and early growth
screens.ans: give young plants suitable conditions for germination and early growth
screens.clue: Think of the early life of a plant.

screens.text: Which are criteria for a good nursery site?
pool: Under the shade of tall trees

screens.text: The best nursery site is perfectly flat.
screens.why: The book says "gently slope": a gentle slope drains water away. (Review Q8 option A wrongly says "flat".)

screens.text: Why should a nursery be shaded from severe sun but NOT placed under big trees?
opts: Seedlings need protection from harsh sun, yet heavy shade and tree roots weaken them
screens.ans: Seedlings need protection from harsh sun, yet heavy shade and tree roots weaken them
screens.why: p.33 asks for protection from severe heat; criterion 8 says not close to shade of trees or buildings. Light shade nets are used instead.

screens.text: Plot A: gentle slope, river nearby, floods every August. Plot B: gentle slope, reliable spring 200 m away, eucalyptus windbreak, open to sun. Plot C: flat, under big trees, near a well. Which is best?
screens.why: A breaks "free from flooding"; C breaks "gently sloping" and "not shaded". B meets the criteria.
screens.clue: Check each plot against the eight criteria.

en.text: Seedlings are raised in nursery beds or in polythene bags; bags often give better seedlings because the tap root is not disturbed, and they save weeding and watering labour. Nursery management starts with the right planting material from the parent plant, then sowing. Seedlings with twisted or poorly developed roots or stems should be discarded; only straight ones are moved to pots or bags. Good nursery care prevents many later problems.

am.text: ችግኞች በፕላስቲክ ከረጢት ሲበቅሉ ዋና ሥራቸው አይረበሽም። የተጣመመ ሥር ወይም ግንድ ያላቸው ችግኞች ይወገዳሉ።

screens.title: Bag or bed?
screens.ask: Seedlings raised in polythene bags often do better after planting than seedlings dug from a bed. Why do you think?
opts: Their main root is not disturbed when moved
screens.after: In a bag the whole root-ball moves with the plant, so the tap root is not torn.

screens.title: Raising seedlings
paras: Seedlings are raised in nursery beds or polythene bags.
Bags often give better seedlings.
The tap root is not disturbed.
Bags save labour for weeding and watering.
Many fruit problems are avoided by good care in the nursery.

screens.title: Managing the nursery
paras: First get the right planting material from the parent plant.
Then sow the seed.
Seedlings emerge soon after.
Some show twisted or poorly developed roots or stems.
Discard them: they rarely become good plants or rootstocks.
Move only straight seedlings to pots or bags.

screens.title: Key word
defs: The main root that grows straight down from the seed.

screens.text: What should be done with seedlings that have twisted roots or stems?
screens.why: p.34: they have very little chance of becoming good plants or rootstocks.

screens.title: Put the nursery work in order
items: Get the right planting material from the parent plant
Fill bags with 2:1:1 soil mix and sow
Water, shade and weed the seedlings
Transplant strong seedlings to the main field
screens.why: Site first, then material, sowing, care, culling, and finally field planting.
screens.clue: What must you have before you can sow?

screens.text: Which are advantages of raising seedlings in polythene bags?
pool: The tap root is not disturbed
a: The tap root is not disturbed

screens.text: Activity: on a nursery visit, which practice would you NOT expect to see?
opts: Keeping twisted seedlings to use as rootstocks
screens.ans: Keeping twisted seedlings to use as rootstocks
screens.why: Twisted seedlings make poor rootstocks and are discarded (p.34).

screens.ask: A nursery fills 400 polythene bags, each with 2 litres of 2:1:1 mix (forest soil : sand : manure). Forest soil needed = ___ litres
screens.why: Total mix = 400 × 2 = 800 L. 4 parts, one part = 200 L. Forest soil = 2 parts = 400 L.

test.text: Which nursery site breaks TWO of the book's criteria?

A gentle slope with a spring
